items.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023
items.q: I was really attracted to unison lines... And then that turned into hearing Chick Corea and his and the Seventh Galaxy... I remember that chapel just like — and I was oh my God man, music can do that... Chick went down to start the second set

ctx.x: Theoretical knowledge you mentioned — I’m curious because we go back a long ways and you come from a small town called Verona, New York, and I remember wondering back then seeing you in this band called Dry Jack, where did you and your brother, how did you come to this music, which at the time we would have — we’ll call it jazz fusion I guess.

Oh the fusion thing. You know man it was like playing — I started playing drums, you know that was my first axe. And then — when I was ten — and that was pretty much, that was it for me as far as the devotion to music. But Rich and I were in bands up until — like for fifteen years straight and we developed musically as we went along and started getting into — you know the fusion thing probably started with stuff we were doing cover tunes like Jeff Beck and we were doing, and then I was in a band called the…
